# Find the Difference of Two Arrays. compare: unordered 1 accepts the values
# of each inner array in any order, but the first array is always nums1's;
# the expected answers below list each array in increasing order.

@example 5 is only in nums1; 0 and 3 are only in nums2; -2 and 8 are in both.
[5,-2,8,5]
[8,3,-2,0]
=> [[5],[0,3]]

@example Both arrays hold the values 1 and 4 and nothing else, so neither has a value of its own.
[1,1,4]
[4,4,1]
=> [[],[]]

@example No value is shared; nums1 repeats 7, but it is listed once.
[7,9,7]
[2]
=> [[7,9],[2]]

# Single elements, equal.
[0]
[0]
=> [[],[]]

# Single elements at the bounds.
[-1000]
[1000]
=> [[-1000],[1000]]

# The bounds, repeated, and a neighbour of one of them.
[-1000,1000,-1000]
[1000,999]
=> [[-1000],[999]]

# nums1's values are all in nums2.
[3,6]
[6,1,3,-4]
=> [[],[-4,1]]

# nums2's values are all in nums1.
[10,-10,20,-20]
[20,-10,20]
=> [[-20,10],[]]

# Repeated values missing from the other array are listed once.
[2,2,2,2,5]
[5,6,6,6]
=> [[2],[6]]

# Repeated values present in the other array are not listed.
[9,9,9,4]
[9,7]
=> [[4],[7]]

# Disjoint arrays with negatives and zero.
[-3,0,-3,-7]
[3,7,3]
=> [[-7,-3,0],[3,7]]

# The two arrays have different differences, so their order matters.
[1,2,3,4,5]
[5,6]
=> [[1,2,3,4],[6]]

# Every entry equal within each array.
[-5,-5,-5]
[-6,-6]
=> [[-5],[-6]]

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
[3]
[-4,5]
=> [[3],[-4,5]]

@gen 2 small
[997]
[1000]
=> [[997],[1000]]

@gen 3 small
[-1]
[2,0,0,1,1,-1,-1]
=> [[],[0,1,2]]

@gen 4 small
[995,998,999,989,999,994]
[989]
=> [[994,995,998,999],[]]

@gen 5 small
[-1000,-1000,-999,-1000,-1000,-999]
[-1000,-998,-999]
=> [[],[-998]]

@gen 6 small
[-995,-995,-995]
[-1000,-997]
=> [[-995],[-1000,-997]]
